narrative.overview:
The page is a sheet of off-white paper printed in near-black ink, and the physics scene is the specimen pinned to it. One large running subject owns the viewport; everything else is a printed instrument around it: a header rule, a row of axis sliders with their ranges and live values, a row of instances, a transport strip. Each parameter is drawn as an axis, so dragging it reads as remapping the specimen rather than editing a form. The system deliberately rejects the three-pane game-engine editor (scene tree, viewport, property grid).

The material is print. Hairline ink rules divide the sheet; the interface has no shadows, no floating panels and no cards. Controls are square-cornered outlined boxes (2px at most), selection is shown by inverting a box to solid ink, and the only round forms are slider thumbs and status dots. A single signal orange marks the one thing to press, where you are, what has focus, and what already exists. Dark mode is not a second theme: it is the same sheet printed in reverse, with the accent lifted slightly so it keeps its punch on black.

The specimen itself is the one place with physical light. Every 3D scene, in the demo app and on the website alike, shares one look: soft sun shadows caught by an invisible ground, low environment light, filmic tone mapping, and a floor that fades into the sunk-paper ground. The sheet is flat; the thing pinned to it is solid. What is not built yet is drawn as a dashed outline in the muted colour, so solid means shipped and dashed means on the way, in the scene, the legend, the tags and the roadmap.

Type is a two-voice specimen. A heavy, tightly tracked grotesk sets words, from the 96px closing headline down to 13px control names; a monospace sets every number, unit, range end, key hint, axis letter, phase number, install command and version string, always with tabular figures, so values hold still while they change.
keyCharacteristics: Paper ground and ink, one signal-orange accent, dark mode as the reversed print.
Grotesk for words, monospace for every number, unit, axis label and key hint.
Hairline rules instead of containers; no UI shadows, no cards, radius 2px at most.
Solid is shipped, dashed muted is on the roadmap: one convention across scene outlines, tags, legend and roadmap rows.
One shared scene look: soft shadows on a shadow-only ground, environment light, ACES tone mapping, fog in the ground colour.
Selected state is ink inversion; orange is reserved for action, location, focus and the shipped mark.
Data colours (four series, three fixed axes) come from one runtime palette shared by scene, charts and readouts.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange means press this, you are here, focus is here, or this exists (shipped). Selection is never orange; it is ink inversion.

rules.name: The Reverse Print Rule
rules.body: Dark mode inverts paper and ink and lifts the accent from #ff4b1f to #ff5a2e. It introduces no new hues and no new surfaces.

rules.name: The Data-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: Series and axis hues appear only as data: a line, a swatch, a body, a callout, an axis label. Never as decoration or a UI state.

rules.name: The Dashed Future Rule
rules.body: Anything not built yet is drawn dashed in the muted colour: dashed outlines in the scene (scene-muted), a dashed left rule on its tag, a 1.5px dashed legend swatch, a dashed row rule on the roadmap. Shipped things are solid, and the shipped mark is orange.

rules.name: The Mono Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every number, unit, range end, key hint, axis letter, phase number, scene tag, shell command and version string is JetBrains Mono with tabular figures. Words are never mono; numbers are never grotesk.

rules.name: The Heavy Title Rule
rules.body: Titles run at 750 with negative tracking (-0.03 to -0.035em), and the loudest headlines (wordmark, landing hero, 404) at 800 down to -0.04em; subheads at 700; body copy stays at 400 and control text at 500-600, so weight alone separates a title from an instrument.

rules.name: The Specimen First Rule
rules.body: The stage takes the largest share of the first viewport; controls sit beneath it, never beside it.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing on the sheet floats. If an interface element needs separation, it gets a rule or the sunk tone, never a shadow. Shadows belong to the scene's bodies, cast by the shared sun onto the shared ground.

rules.name: The Square Control, Round Thumb Rule
rules.body: Controls are boxes with at most 2px corners; only the thing you drag, and the status dot, is round.

dos: **Do** keep Signal Orange to the primary action, the current-location bar or underline, focus, the dragged thumb, link underlines and the shipped mark.
**Do** show selection by inverting to ink with paper text.
**Do** set every number, unit, range end and key hint in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
**Do** separate regions with a 1px ink rule or hairline (2px ink to open a website section), and use sunk paper as the only tonal step.
**Do** draw anything not yet built as a dashed outline in the muted colour, and anything shipped solid.
**Do** build every 3D view on the shared stage so light, shadow, tone mapping and fog match everywhere.
